title: Brynmere retail LLM call wiring notes
content:
Call summary (2026-03-10)
Attendees: Brynmere - Jess Carter (Head of Product), Omar Ruiz (Platform), Priya Sharma (Security); Redwood - Maya (CS), Samir (Solutions Eng), Lena (SRE).

Purpose: Quick technical sync to align on integration approach for Brynmere's in-store returns assistant and post-purchase recommendations. Goal is a 6-week pilot with production-like traffic replay to validate latency and cost.

High-level ask from Brynmere:
- Build a returns/resolution assistant that integrates with POS and order DB; must return an answer within 250ms p95 for in-store kiosk flow (soft target during pilot: 300ms).
- Support semantic search over product catalogs and customer order history for context (embeddings + vector store).
- No customer PII leaving Brynmere network; they prefer Redwood Private deployed into their AWS account (VPC) or an on-prem option behind HSM/KMS for keys.
- Need ability to fall back to a smaller local policy model when Redwood capacity constrained (offline fallback).

Notes on technical constraints and preferences:
- Traffic profile: spikes during returns windows (typical POS concurrency 80–120 reqs/min peak across 120 stores), avg request payloads modest (60–150 tokens). They will run batch replay of 10k sessions for pilot.
- Regulatory: retail loyalty IDs and partial payment tokens considered sensitive; must be redacted before hitting any hosted inference path. They want guidance on redaction layer and sample regex/policy.
- Vector store: they plan to use AWS OpenSearch + kNN initially, but are open to a managed vector option. Need embedding dimensionality and indexing recommendations (we suggested 1536 embeddings, quantized int8 storage for economy).
- Model choices: prefer an open LLM (Llama 2 variant or Mistral equivalent) with 8-bit quantized variant; suggested runtime path: redwood-llama-13b-8q for cost/latency balance, fallback to smaller 3B family for extreme tails.
- Caching: high reuse expected for common SKU questions; propose prefix/KV cache at Redwood edge and short TTL (30s) for kiosk flows.

Key gotchas called out on the call:
1) Tokenization mismatch between product metadata (special characters in SKUs) and model tokenizer — may drop important tokens. Action: need a normalization step and sample tokenization test script.
2) Embedding drift: product catalog updates hourly; index staleness will surface as poor rerank. Recommend incremental indexing pipeline and a TTL window.
3) Privacy gating: they will not permit full order text in prompts; need to craft redacted summary templates that preserve utility.
4) Latency tail risk: stores on cellular failover paths may have high network latency — plan for local model fallback and prefetching embeddings for recent orders.
5) Cost sensitivity: finance already flagged token budget; show expected unit costs for pilot (per 1M tokens) with Redwood hosted vs private reserved GPUs.

Actionable requirements (explicit) from Brynmere:
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms (target) during steady-state, p99 under 700ms with fallback allowed.
- Security: Deploy Redwood Private in their AWS account with VPC peering and CMK-managed keys. Audit logs forwarded to their SIEM (CloudWatch/Datadog).
- Data residency: customer-generated embeddings and index must remain in their VPC.
- Observability: per-route latency/cost dashboards; want token-level breakdown and KV cache hit rates.
- Rollout: Canary first in 5 pilot stores, then 50 store ramp after perf verification.

Immediate next steps (owners + dates)
- Maya: prepare an integration checklist + sample prompt redaction patterns (regex examples) by 2026-03-15.
- Samir: prototype tokenization test harness for SKUs/descriptions and run against candidate model tokenizers; deliver report by 2026-03-18.
- Lena: draft private deployment network diagram (VPC flow, peering, subnet mapping) and required IAM roles; due 2026-03-16.
- Omar (Brynmere): provide 2 weeks of sanitized replay traffic (anonymized tokens & order metadata) by 2026-03-20.
- Priya (Brynmere): confirm KMS/HSM constraints and list approved CAs for certs by 2026-03-14.
- Joint: schedule a pilot kickoff (engineering deep-dive) week of 2026-03-22; Samir to lead technical agenda.

Proposed pilot architecture (short)
1) Data plane in Brynmere VPC: order DB + sanitized replay events + OpenSearch index for product vectors.
2) Redwood Private control plane (managed) with serving nodes in Brynmere VPC via private subnets. CMK keys for encryption.
3) Edge redaction proxy runs in Brynmere infra to sanitize PII before requests reach Redwood.
4) Fallback local model container (3B quantized) deployed to edge kiosk for < 50ms local inference when network degraded.

Risk register (initial)
- Tokenization / SKU mis-splits => wrong retrieval (mitigation: normalization + test harness).
- Embedding staleness causing rerank regressions (mitigation: incremental re-index + freshness TTL).
- Unexpected cost overrun in pilot due to prompt verbosity (mitigation: cost simulation, prompt compression, n_ctx caps).
- Approval delays on security certs (mitigation: escalate via enterprise sales).

Notes to self / informal TODOs
- Build a short demo prompt set that shows privacy-preserving examples (mask/summary) vs raw order text so Brynmere security can evaluate utility.
- Put together quick TCO slide comparing Redwood Dedicated reserved nodes vs Private-in-VPC runbook (include GPU flavors and estimated token throughput).
- Add an item to JIRA (JIRA-9821) to track embedding reindex automation work.

Open questions for next call
- Brynmere: Are they fixed on OpenSearch or would a managed Redis/PG-based vector store be acceptable?
- Security: exact retention policy for raw logs — do they want 30d or 90d?
- Ops: who will own the fallback local model image updates at stores? Brynmere or Redwood SRE?

Meeting artifacts to attach to pilot folder
- sample sanitized replay file (when Omar uploads)
- tokenization test results CSV (Samir)
- private deployment network diagram (Lena)

Quick agenda for engineering kickoff (proposed)
- 15m: goals & success metrics (product)
- 30m: data and privacy review (security)
- 45m: infra architecture and deployment plan (SRE + solutions eng)
- 30m: model & prompt design (applied ML)
- 20m: next steps & milestone calendar


End of notes — rough and scribbly, will refine into a formal pilot brief once we have replay data and Priya's security constraints.
